tasks.title: Populate rootfs payloads with Linux-owned metadata
tasks.goal: Assemble an offline Linux rootfs through the already prepared executor while preserving target filesystem semantics.
steps: Consume exact Vibe payload and selected backend closure from M-15-A/E inside the M-15-K worker; do not bootstrap the worker here.
Map target principals, files/directories/safe links/modes into an owned rootfs and emit a complete independent metadata inventory.
Validate host/target path separation and unsupported privileged metadata before writes; verify resulting Linux executables and links using target tools.
positive_cases: POSIX executable mode and target-root symlink semantics survive Windows-controlled assembly.
Inventory matches realized files and declared runtime closure.
negative_cases: Windows host identity is used as Linux UID/GID.
Rootfs extraction follows a target absolute link into the host.
checks: TO CREATE: Linux rootfs metadata/ABI inventory integration test using the existing commissioned worker.
acceptance: The rootfs is target-correct with independently observed metadata.
No target binary runs on the wrong architecture or directly in the Windows controller.
tasks.safe_stop: An offline rootfs candidate and manifest are retained; no host service or deployment starts.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(rootfs): populate Linux payloads with target metadata
notes: Planned permanent destination: vibevm/vibespecs/common/PROP-065-oci-agent-images.xml; forward metadata only.
The environment/ module is a proposed composition cell in the existing orchestrator; its owning export file is included for registration. Refine the perimeter before touching any additional crate.

Use full listed crate tests by default. If narrowing to a newly created test filter, first run cargo test -p <crate> -- --list and verify an exact nonzero test-name match; a zero-test run is not acceptance.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Bind backend hooks and offline service preparation
tasks.goal: Keep guest-root package effects inside the exact offline target and separate installation from service startup.
steps: Bind backend config, DB, cache, keyring and hook context to the intended rootfs; encode the selected root/sysroot behavior explicitly.
Separate emitted service/account/config definitions from live startup actions; admit only target-bound preparation effects.
Exercise a hook writing a permitted target resource and a disallowed host/service effect; return structured partial/error evidence and exact cleanup ownership.
positive_cases: Offline preparation produces declared target configuration without starting services.
A legitimate admitted hook changes only the captured target footprint.
negative_cases: A hook writes the controller's HOME or starts a host daemon.
Offline population is reported as proof of running or healthy services.
checks: TO CREATE: offline-hook containment and no-host-service integration fixture.
acceptance: All observed preparation effects belong to the target transaction domains.
Live activation remains a separate operation and authority.
tasks.safe_stop: Offline target is complete or explicitly incomplete; all external service state is unchanged.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(rootfs): separate offline preparation from live service effects
